chapter: Sanger, Ben Black and carnival balls
title: Pinky Vodakovich at a Biloxi ball
summary: He recounts booking Pinky Vodakovich to entertain at a Biloxi ball and his song Arizay.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: He was going to ask you, I could get your checks with him. Sure. He was Pinky Vodakovich. Remember Pinky? Sure. Pinky was a clever boy. Not much of a musician, but very clever. I brought him over to Bluxley to play a strip. We had a ball, the title of which was Shrimp Boats. They always said, Johnny, you're in New Orleans, you're getting more entertainment. Get us some entertainment. So I said, well now Pinky would be ideal because he has that accent. He's from down in Buras, you know. So Pinky comes over there dressed like a shrimp fisherman. He wouldn't dress. Faded dungarees, a blue turtleneck sweater, and a knitted cap. I guess they thought he was some bum, but he was dressed in character. And he tells these boogaloo jokes, and the people in Biloxi don't talk that way. They don't know anything about the Cajun language. No. No, they don't. They're shrimp pickers. But this ball wasn't shrimp pickers. It was a high class ball because they wouldn't have had that kind of money. I gave Pinky a hundred bucks to do it in about five minutes. And he's dying out there. I said, it's the wrong thing. I broke the wrong thing. So he looks at me, I said, sing. He says, all right folks, I'm going to sing my own composition, Arizay. You remember he wrote Arizay? Sure. And my piano player says, where's the music? Pinky comes in with our music, of all people, our band. But the band knew Arizay, so we went into Arizay and we played it for him. Piano player faked up and we're keeping all that good time, you're listening to all that
